solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slight breaks alarming

indicators.note: breaks tells us the word alarming is smashed up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A small crack in something turns out to be worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' reads as a noun with 'alarming' as its verb, but it is the anagram signal acting on ALARMING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marginal is small or minor in amount, just as a slight difference is.

clue.text: Under yours truly, every king initially submissive

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means the initials sit below the speaker's word

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, me

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of every and of king

explanation.surface: The speaker says every king below them is docile.
explanation.definitionFit: A meek person is quiet and gentle, readily submitting to others.

clue.text: Book substitute

definitions.meaning: to book is to ... a table or seat
a substitute player, as on a team bench

explanation.definitionFit: Booking a seat means reserving it; a substitute player is a reserve.

clue.text: Popular knight, one on list for sure

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the one sits above the list

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to dub someone is to knight them with a sword tap
I is the Roman numeral one
a table is a list of figures

explanation.surface: A well-liked knight is certainly one on the honours list.
explanation.definitionFit: Indubitable means beyond doubt, certain, as something known for sure.

clue.text: Revolting part, I'm hollow

indicators.note: revolting letters rise up and overturn their order

explanation.surface: Someone admits one body part is disgusting and they feel empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like the adjective 'disgusting' but signals rearranging PART and IM.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the shoulder where arm meets body.

clue.text: God snatching gold from writer

indicators.note: snatching gold from the writer means the letters for gold are taken away from that word

parts.note: a writer is an author
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A deity steals precious metal from a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder, who wields the hammer Mjolnir.

clue.text: Island nation — it is secured by endless locks

indicators.note: the word it is held fast inside the shortened locks
endless means the last letter is cut from the locks word

parts.note: locks are hair
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Caribbean country, guarded by locks without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door fastenings, but here it means hair; 'is' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean country on the island of Hispaniola.

clue.text: Useless designer stepped down

indicators.note: a useless arrangement is a bad one, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An incompetent designer quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resigned is to have given up a post, to have stepped down.

clue.text: Leaders in every Asian state evidently drowsy, relaxed

indicators.note: the leaders of the following words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: Every Asian state seems sleepy and laid back.
explanation.definitionFit: To have eased something is to have loosened or relaxed it; both are past-tense verbs.

clue.text: Parents, those kept under wraps?

definitions.meaning: mothers, in the familiar British spelling, who are one kind of parent
embalmed Egyptian bodies bound in linen bandages, literally kept under wraps

explanation.definitionFit: Mothers are parents; embalmed bodies wrapped in linen strips are quite literally kept under wraps.

clue.text: Wandering free, man and kids become buddies

indicators.note: wandering letters roam about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A free-roaming man and some children strike up a friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' only joins: the rearranged letters are FREE, MAN and KIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To make friends is to form a friendship, to become pals.

clue.text: Excitement of member in cage, very amusing

indicators.note: X of Y here puts the member word in front of the excitement word

parts.note: a rib is one member of the rib cage
tickling is a stirring or excitement of the senses

explanation.surface: Something thrilling happens to a body part inside a cage, and it's hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives TICKLING 'of' RIB, so read it as RIB-TICKLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib-tickling joke is one so funny it makes you laugh hard.

clue.text: Listed site, heading off, is in sea

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of site
in places the word is inside the sea word

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A listed building, its sign removed, sits in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A listed building in Britain is one protected for its historic interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Itemised means set out item by item, as in a list.

clue.text: Contract put away, attempt to steal it

indicators.note: the attempt word steals the other piece, taking it inside itself

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: An agreement is shelved, then someone tries to pinch it.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states, a kind of contract.

clue.text: Apartment in Odense gutted recently

indicators.note: in places the apartment word inside the other letters
gutted means the insides of Odense are removed, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

explanation.surface: A flat in the Danish city of Odense has been stripped out lately.
explanation.walkthrough: Odense is a city in Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late is an idiom meaning lately or in recent times.

clue.text: Regalia manufactured for African country

indicators.note: manufactured letters are made up again into another form

explanation.surface: Royal insignia produced for a nation in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is the largest country in Africa, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: River mammal going after river rat!

indicators.note: going after puts the mammal after the river letter

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
an otter is a mammal living by rivers

explanation.surface: An otter chases a water rat.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the surprise of 'rat' being a person, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is a contemptible person, a rat or cad.

clue.text: Be wary of huffing and puffing, staggering

parts.note: to mind something is to be careful of it, as in mind the gap
blowing hard, like the wolf in the fairy tale

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for someone panting and reeling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mind-blowing is astonishing, overwhelming, staggering.

clue.text: Feature about right for old language

indicators.note: about puts the facial feature around the right letter

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A characteristic correct for an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the language of the medieval Scandinavians and Vikings.

clue.text: Trainer possibly has month to improve, all concluding

indicators.note: the concluding letters of all four words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A coach is given a month to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: A trainer here is a sports shoe (a sneaker), not a coach; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is one example of footwear, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Excess strife, worried about university

indicators.note: about puts the scrambled letters around the university letter
worried letters are disturbed and shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Too much conflict and anxiety on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges STRIFE into SRFEIT, and 'about' wraps that round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an oversupply, more than is needed.

clue.text: Some pin, or this point

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Choosing which pin to use, this one or that.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal point of the compass, one of the four main directions.

clue.text: Eat less — stop before end of dessert!

indicators.note: before puts the stop word ahead of the final letter

parts.note: an engine that dies stops

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word dessert

explanation.surface: Advice to a dieter: cut down and skip pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: To diet is to restrict what you consume, usually to lose weight.

clue.text: Antipodean capital turning Serbian, alongside capital in Belgrade

indicators.note: alongside sets the single letter next to the rearranged word
the capital in Belgrade is its first, capital, letter
turning means Serbian is turned over into a different order

explanation.surface: A Serbian leaves Belgrade and becomes an Australian city dweller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges SERBIAN into RISBANE. Brisbane is the state capital of Queensland, not a national capital, so 'Antipodean capital' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisbane is the capital city of Queensland, in Australia, a land of the antipodes.
